title: P2P Capability Ledger Schema
description: Canonical machine-readable record of P2P capabilities: knowledge, status, and roadmap intent. This ledger is NOT a runtime truth store, NOT Task State, and NOT a second FACT store. It does not control runtime task completion.

ledger_id.description: Stable identifier of this ledger file, matching its filename.

schema_version.description: Bump when the record shape changes; older records are migrated or preserved in history.

canonical_source_statement.description: Declares the canonical sources this ledger is derived from. This is the drift-protection header: derived artifacts must declare their source.
examples: Derived from governance/development-control.json (roadmap, architectural_invariants, candidate_records), docs/AI-HANDOFF.md, docs/KIEN-TRUC.md, and per-goal evidence. Not a copy of FACT ledger or Task State.

authority_boundary.description: Encodes the boundary: what this ledger does and does not control.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of last reconciliation. Roadmap projection (current-roadmap.md) is deterministically derived from this file.

families.description: Family registry. Each family id maps to a human name and a one-line purpose. Family ids used in capabilities must be registered here.

status_vocabulary.description: The only allowed capability statuses. Do not invent additional labels.

capabilities.description: Capability records. capability_id must be unique.

capability_id.description: Unique machine identifier. Existing ledger-native IDs use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE; canonical runtime capability IDs retain lowercase dotted identity.

family.description: Must be a key registered in families.

beginner_value.description: Answers 'What technical burden does this remove from a non-coder?' in owner-facing terms. Required for every material capability. Bad example: 'Adds host resolver.' Good example: 'Owner no longer needs to know which AI can safely perform the task.'

principle.description: Charter invariant this capability serves, e.g. BEGINNER_FIRST, PROJECT_STATE_NOT_CHAT_HISTORY.

origin_refs.description: Recoverable origin: goal documents, plans, reports, research notes. If origin cannot be durably recovered, use exactly 'origin_unknown_or_not_durably_recovered'. Do not fabricate precise origins.

origin_type.description: Categorical origin class. IMPLEMENTATION_GOAL = born from a durable implementation Goal. RESEARCH_DECISION = born from the research decision registry. OWNER_ACCEPTED_PROPOSAL = born from owner-accepted chat/context proposals; it MUST enter the roadmap as PLANNED and is NOT an implementation. ARCHITECTURE_INVARIANT = born from a charter invariant or structural requirement. UPSTREAM_SPECIFICATION = born from an upstream host/spec requirement. PROJECT_LEARNING = born from evaluation or learning history. REJECTED_DESIGN = a rejected pattern kept on the ledger to prevent reintroduction. RECOVERED_LEGACY = reconstructed from recovered legacy artifacts (evidence-only). UNKNOWN = origin cannot be durably recovered; origin_refs must then be exactly ['origin_unknown_or_not_durably_recovered'].

evidence_refs.description: Behavioral evidence: test files, QA/coder/supervisor reports, candidate zips, evals. REQUIRED when status is VERIFIED_IMPLEMENTED.

dependencies.description: capability_ids this record depends on; each must reference a valid capability_id in this ledger. The field itself is REQUIRED: an empty list is a valid declaration meaning 'no dependencies'. Dependency intent must always be explicitly declared, never implied by absence.

known_gaps.description: What is still missing or intentionally out of scope.

do_not_duplicate_with.description: capability_ids or subsystems this must not be reimplemented as.

next_condition.description: When this capability should be reconsidered or what must be true before work resumes.

roadmap_relation.description: Truthful relation to an existing roadmap item or an explicit deferral. Must not imply a roadmap row, adoption state, or Owner authorization that does not exist.

deferred_reason.description: Why it was deferred, when known. Required when status is DEFERRED.

rejected_reason.description: Why it must not be reintroduced. Required when status is REJECTED.
